specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** workshop-problem-solver
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** recommend
**Learning Objective:** The learner will recommend the best response to each of six problems that arise during a workshop day, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Facilitator Guide, Workshop Agenda, Teacher Training Workshop (all defined in this chapter above this block), and the privacy and licensing chapters (Chapters 2 and 13). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each problem the learner chooses one of three responses. A choice is correct when it matches the Best response column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the guide excerpt is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The schedule must be kept at any cost. (2) A real resource from a teacher can be pasted into any tool. (3) A participant's licensing question can wait until after the workshop. **Instructional Rationale:** Recommending a response to a live problem is an Evaluate-level action. Problems that involve time, tools, privacy, and licensing teach the learner what a facilitator guide must anticipate. **Content:** The six problems (all made up), each with three responses: | # | Problem | Responses | Best response | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Three teachers cannot log in to the agent tool at 8:45. | A: Pause the whole room until all three are fixed. B: Pair each of the three with a neighbor who is logged in, and fix the logins during the first break. C: Tell them to try again at home. | B | Pairing keeps the room moving and the fix happens in parallel. | | 2 | A teacher wants to paste a class roster with student names into the agent to score a quiz. | A: Allow it, since the teacher owns the data. B: Stop it, remind the room that student data stays out of prompts, and use the sample quiz. C: Ask the teacher to remove only the last names. | B | Student information stays out of the prompt, as Chapter 13 taught. | | 3 | The calibration session runs 20 minutes over. | A: Cut the checking-the-agent session in half. B: Shorten the break and move one calibration comparison to a take-home task. C: Skip lunch. | B | It protects the sessions that depend on each other without cutting a core skill. | | 4 | A teacher's resource turns out to have no license. | A: Improve it anyway and publish it as CC BY. B: Switch that teacher to the sample resource for the improvement challenge, and have them ask the owner for permission later. C: Tell them to add a CC BY license themselves. | B | Without a license, only the owner can allow an improved version. | | 5 | Two teachers and the agent disagree by 5 points on Accessibility. | A: Average the three scores. B: Ask each to show their evidence and decide which one the evidence supports. C: Use the agent's score because it is faster. | B | Disagreements are settled by the evidence, as Chapters 11 and 14 taught. | | 6 | A participant says the agent's score is obviously wrong but cannot say why. | A: Ask them to find the check that the agent passed and that they believe fails, and test it. B: Agree and move on. C: Tell them the agent is usually right. | A | Turning a hunch into a specific check is how the finding gets verified. | **Provenance:** The problems are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The responses follow Chapters 11, 13, 14, and 15. **Rules:** Each problem has exactly one best response. The sim shuffles the order of the three responses for each problem, so that the letter shown does not give away the answer. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one problem and its three responses. 2. The learner chooses a response, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was best and the Why text. 4. After problem 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 problems in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [response]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The best response is [response]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can handle a workshop day." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed problem. **Starting State:** The first problem in the shuffled order and its three responses. The question shown is "What is the best response?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a facilitator guide includes the common problems with their fixes.
